findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (and add an AC/test for) the fetch=True / review-plan path staying correct under the new tracker-HEAD-first pin resolution.
evidence: 'resolves the snapshot sha from the tracker repo HEAD when that repo is present, falling back to the existing origin/tickets -> local-branch chain'
Root cause 1: 'review-plan ... passes no fetch flag, so it defaults to True'
No AC covers review-plan's continued correctness under the new resolution order
findings.finding: Step 1 changes materialize_tickets to resolve the pin from the tracker-repo HEAD 'when that repo is present' for ALL callers, but review-plan already calls with fetch=True and currently pins origin/tickets; the plan does not confirm the new tracker-HEAD-first resolution leaves the fetch=True (review-plan) path behaving correctly, so a cross-consumer regression is neither ruled out nor covered by a criterion.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 1 vs Root cause 1 ('review-plan ... defaults to True')
scenarios: A close-time host where tracker HEAD and origin/tickets diverge: review-plan (fetch=True) now reads tracker HEAD instead of origin/tickets and sees a different snapshot than before
findings.suggested_fix: Add a regression assertion covering the fetch=True caller and state in step 1 whether tracker-HEAD-first applies to fetch=True or only fetch=False.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the fetch=True consumer (review-plan / verify-completion via resolve_gate_handle) and state whether the new tracker-HEAD-first resolution changes what it pins, or explicitly scope the resolution change to the fetch=False path only.
evidence: materialize_tickets is called from resolve_gate_handle with fetch threaded from the caller: 'tickets_root = materialize_tickets(repo_root=repo_root, fetch=fetch)' (gate_source.py:115)

The current fetch=True branch deliberately prefers <remote>/<ref>: 'if fetch and has_remote(...): sha = resolve_ref(f"{remote}/{ref}"...)' to 'pin the SHARED store, not a stale local copy' (repo_snapshot.py:554-572)

Plan step 1 says the tracker-HEAD pin 'makes fetch=False harmless' but does not state how the fetch=True (review-plan) resolution is affected by preferring '.tickets-tracker HEAD when that repo is present'
findings.finding: Step 1 modifies the shared resolution logic of materialize_tickets for ALL callers, but only the close (fetch=False) path is analyzed; the review-plan/verify-completion caller that invokes it with fetch=True (via resolve_gate_handle in gate_source.py:115, reached from operations.py) is not enumerated as an affected consumer, even though the change re-bases the pin from the origin/tickets->local-branch chain onto tracker-repo HEAD.
findings.location: Implementation plan, step 1 ('Pin the ticket store at the LIVE store's own HEAD'); src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:568-576; src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:115
scenarios: A review-plan run (fetch=True) on a host where local .tickets-tracker HEAD lags the pushed origin/tickets: the new tracker-HEAD-first rule could pin the local tracker HEAD instead of the shared origin ref, changing review-plan's pinned view.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in Fix 1 which git object store materialize_tickets reads the tracker-HEAD SHA and tree from (the .tickets-tracker repo, not root_dir), and confirm _materialize_tree/_ensure_blobs_present are pointed at that repo so the chosen SHA's tree is guaranteed reachable without a network fetch.
evidence: Plan: 'materialize_tickets resolves the snapshot sha from the tracker repo (.tickets-tracker) HEAD ... needs no network, keeps the snapshot immutable and signable'
repo_snapshot.py:590-591: `_ensure_blobs_present(root_dir, sha, remote)` then `_materialize_tree(root_dir, sha, tracker)` — both keyed to root_dir (the main repo), not the tracker repo
Plan's own RC1: the main repo's local refs/heads/tickets 'only advances on fetch' and is '6757 commits behind' — so a tracker-HEAD SHA is by construction likely absent from the main repo's object DB
findings.finding: Fix 1 sources the pinned SHA from the separate .tickets-tracker repo's HEAD but does not specify which object store materialize_tickets reads that commit's tree from; the main repo's object DB (which _materialize_tree/_ensure_blobs_present operate against via root_dir) is ~6757 commits behind and may not contain the tracker-HEAD commit or its blobs, so materialization could fail with the very SHA the fix chooses.
scenarios: Tracker repo HEAD is far ahead of the main repo's tickets mirror; close-precheck pins tracker HEAD but _materialize_tree cannot find that tree in root_dir's objects, so the pin fails or the cache-by-SHA path materializes an incomplete tree.
findings.suggested_fix: State that when .tickets-tracker is present, both the SHA resolution AND the tree materialization (rev-parse, ls-tree, blob presence) run against the tracker repo's own object DB (git -C .tickets-tracker), reserving root_dir/origin only for the fallback chain.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving check for AC5 (grep/assert the prompt and remediation strings say 'not visible in the ticket snapshot' and no longer assert 'does not exist').
evidence: Step 3 changes the verifier prompt and remediation guidance wording but lists no test
Step 5 (regression tests) names only the stale-tickets fixture and the empty-findings verdict test
findings.finding: AC5 (distinguish 'not present' from 'not visible in the snapshot read') maps only to prose-wording changes in step 3 and has no named proving command or regression test, unlike AC3 and AC4 which do.
scenarios: The wording revert is partially applied (prompt updated, remediation guidance missed) and no check catches it
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 5 a test that asserts the emitted diagnostic/remediation text contains the 'not visible in the snapshot' phrasing and not the 'does not exist' phrasing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact representation of the 'no verdict obtainable' state in the completion_verdict contract (a new `verdict` token vs. a separate flag), and specify how it passes through `_norm_verdict` (contracts.py:145), `reconcile_verdict` (completion.py:454), the eval scorer's PASS/FAIL check (eval_scorers.py:161), and the finalizer prompt.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'a non-PASS verdict carrying zero findings AND zero criteria is recorded as indeterminate rather than as a fabricated unmet criterion' and 'The verdict still blocks the close (fail-closed is preserved).'
contracts.py:145 `_norm_verdict`: `return "PASS" if str(v).strip().upper() == "PASS" else "FAIL"` — any non-PASS verdict token (including 'INDETERMINATE') coerces to FAIL at schema-validation time.
completion.py:454-455 `reconcile_verdict`: `verdict = "PASS" if raw == "PASS" else "FAIL"` — the same coercion in the reconciler the plan is editing.
eval_scorers.py:161 `_schema_verdict`: `if verdict not in {"PASS", "FAIL"}: return ScoreResult(True, False, ...)` — the completion_verdict eval contract rejects any third token.
Contrast: plan-review uses PASS|BLOCK|INDETERMINATE (e.g. plan_review/__init__.py:435), a defined third-value vocabulary; completion_verdict has no such token defined.

The plan does not state whether indeterminacy is a new `verdict` token, a separate boolean/field on completion_verdict, or purely a close_precheck-side classification — so the executor cannot know the representation.
findings.finding: Step 2 introduces an 'indeterminate' / 'no verdict obtainable' state for completion verification but never defines how it is represented in the completion_verdict structured-output contract whose verdict vocabulary is exactly {PASS, FAIL} — and three separate points coerce/validate any non-PASS token back to FAIL.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; AC line 'A non-PASS verdict with no itemized criteria is reported as "no verdict obtainable"'
scenarios: Executor of step 2 emits verdict='INDETERMINATE' and it is silently coerced to FAIL by _norm_verdict / reconcile_verdict, defeating the distinct-channel goal.
Executor adds a third verdict token; the completion_verdict eval scorer (_schema_verdict) then fails the contract as 'not in PASS/FAIL'.
close_precheck at line 543 keys solely on verdict != PASS; without a defined field it cannot tell an indeterminate result from an ordinary FAIL to choose exit 11 vs 1.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether indeterminacy is carried as a new field (e.g. `verdict=FAIL` plus a distinct `verdict_class='indeterminate'`/`no_verdict` marker, preserving the {PASS,FAIL} enum and fail-closed blocking) or a third verdict token; if the latter, enumerate the required updates to _norm_verdict, reconcile_verdict, _schema_verdict, and the completion_verifier/finalizer prompts so the token is not coerced away. close_precheck then reads that marker to choose exit 11 vs 1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the consumers of close_precheck's exit code and confirm they treat exit 11 as retryable (with a rollback note if the 1->11 change breaks any).
evidence: 'exits retryable (11) instead of a bare FAIL (1)'
T4 requires a consumer-facing behavior change be acknowledged with a rollback/expand-contract path, not just asserted safe
findings.finding: The fix changes close_precheck's exit-code contract (bare FAIL exit 1 becomes retryable exit 11 for the indeterminate case), but the plan does not enumerate consumers of that exit code (CI wrapper, calling scripts, retry harness) nor confirm they treat 11 as retryable, and states no rollback/back-out path for the behavior change.
scenarios: A CI job or retry loop keyed on exit 1 as 'hard fail' now sees 11 and either loops forever or treats it as success
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC/step that names the exit-code consumers (CI, retry harness) and asserts exit 11 is handled as retryable; state the current-vs-new mapping explicitly.
